newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing debt market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing debt market report.

text.p: Dutch bonds closed down but above their lowest intraday levels, tracking Bunds in extremely thin volume.
"This is the most boring day of the year," said one dealer, adding he was unsure why market players were unmoved.
"This morning, quietness could be blamed on Monday morning meetings, but trade did not pick up later either," he said.

He said the school holidays in the Netherlands and anxiety over Federal Reserve Board chairman Alan Greenspan's semi-annual testimony on the state of the U.S. economy to Congress later this week did not justify the extent of the market's slackness.
The Dutch yield curve steepened somewhat during the day, as short bonds outperformed longer paper.
But because of the very light volumes, traders did not attribute the steepening of the curve to a particular trend.
One said there had been some switching out of 2007 and into 2006 guilder bonds, adding he had also heard of traders selling Bunds and buying guilder bonds in the very short end.
Dealers said the main subject market players focussed on during the day was whether the Dutch central bank would decide to hike its special advances rate on Thursday.
"The guilder has further weakened against the mark, crossing the essential 1.1235 level. This set afloat renewed talk of a rate hike," one dealer said.

Rabobank International said in its Financial Weekly report that it expected a unilateral hike in the special advances rate this week. Rabobank analyst Niels Kortleve told Reuters he expected a rise of 10-20 basis points in the advances rate.
The special advances rate has been held at 2.50 percent since August. The repo rate currently stands at 3.00 percent.
The special advances rate and the repo rate set the tone for money market rates in each country.
